_lead: Battle gear of this age: this is the age of beasts and newborn gods, long before any empire, when magic is taken by hand from slain monsters (their elemental cores forged into blades, their hides still carrying frost, fire or lightning), from dwarven runes hammered into iron, from altar miracles and from cold white pale-silver fire, so battle gear here looks like gear from a fantasy JRPG of that world, not plain medieval or stone-age kit. The description above already sets how much gear this character wears, from rank, wealth and taste: follow it exactly. Where it says plain, simple, unadorned or no armour, keep it that way; this note only supplies the look of the pieces it names. No electric lights, no modern clothes,
夜祷: no gunpowder, no firearms (dwarven red-core blasting tubes open mountains, never battles). Pale silver has reached the armour: highland heavy cavalry in bronze-hide lamellar pressed from bronze-wolf hide, a seven-ringed wall burnt on the chest, plates dusted with pale-silver powder that flash into one sheet of cold white light in the charge, horses draped in bronze-wolf pelts; kings and dukes in gilded breastplates with silver-plated crowns, pauldrons and sword guards gleaming cold; after the throne falls, noble house riders with their stone-city crest chiselled on the plates and the silver light growing dimmer; beast hunters with core-forged blades and a sealed silver core-jar at the belt; academy initiates from the southern ring mountains with a single pale-silver ring that links spells; rebel mine slaves in torn hemp with broken shackles and ore hammers.
晚祷下: no gunpowder, no firearms. A treaty age, gear marked with oaths rather than victories: lake-kingdom knights over mail with tall tower shields painted with a ring of water and one star, ash-wood spears with a bridge lantern hung from the shaft, the ring of water and the oath lines on the plate glowing when the vow is spoken; squires carrying a blank, unpainted tower shield; the lake king's sword hilt set with a shard of a lake-bottom stone ring that glows pale teal at night; beast-eared couriers in grey cloaks with one feather at the collar, no weapon but a knife; field healers in undyed white linen, no armour, palms faintly warm with miracle light; the war's core-forged blades and engraved plate still worn, but sheathed.
晚祷上: no gunpowder, no firearms. Three centuries of the seven kings' war, decided by champions standing between the armies: heroes in armour and weapons made from slain beast lords, a lord-horn battle-axe that lifts stone chips into the air when raised; sun-kingdom knights in polished overlapping plate with a gold crown on the breast and sun-rays that catch a holy glow, lances with narrow pennons, squires in leather branded with a crown; hired blades with core-forged swords that trail flame and arrows that frost the wound, the richer the paymaster the more fire-colour; mountain pass guards holding a rock-breath, skin hard as stone; highland heavy cavalry in bronze-hide armour on wolf-pelted horses; steppe riders with lance, short bow and saddle round shield; dwarven round shields whose rune ring burns red under fire.
午祷下: no gunpowder, no firearms. Crowns and hilts crowded with rubies and pale star-stones: nobles and knights with gem-set sword guards and gauntlets whose star-stones flare when gripped, empty settings where gems were pawned for grain; town guards in leather branded with the town crest, straw-coloured spear tassels; on the grasslands no armies, beast-eared hunters fight with their own bodies, fur vests, bone whistles, short bows and hounds, clan marks burnt into the leather; highland hunters whose long blades leave a gust of green wind; a storm rider's seamless hemp rein whose white fibres stand up and spark with thin lightning; caravan guards with core-forged short spears and cloth-stuffed bells.
午祷上: no gunpowder, no firearms (dwarven red blasting powder only opens mountains). Bought gems in crowns, but beast cores still forged into weapons: thunder hunters in storm-wolf hide cloaks whose lightning pattern glows purple and grounds the strike into the earth, bone knives, no iron, nail-less soft boots; the copper king's crown with a sparking purple thunder core ringed with rubies; dwarven iron shields struck with runes that blaze into a ring of fire-light and turn a dragon's breath; knights painting their lord's arms on shields, horses barded in bronze hide; dragon-hunters in hard leather buttoned to the chin with a curved bleeding knife; hiding dragonblood folk with a faint red glow behind the high collar.
晨祷: no gunpowder, no firearms. Gods have just sat down at their altars and every treasure is self-slain: highland lords with a glowing beast core set in crown, helm or shield boss, bronze house badges mixed with core dust that answer only their owner; heavy cavalry in bronze-hide lamellar on horses draped in bronze-wolf pelts, thundering in the charge; beast slayers with fire-mane bone greatswords trailing flame and frost-fang arrowheads, northern miners with rock-breath skin; heroes worth a thousand soldiers; temple guards with altar-blessed white cords that shine softly, priests unarmoured with candle-flame miracle light; lamplighters' long poles tipped with pale-silver white fire that drives back monster vines.
万兽后: no gunpowder, no firearms, no steel plate. Small kingdoms, each with its colour and its beast: thunder-country soldiers carry no iron, blue-glazed ceramic helms, dry wooden spears and big shields of storm-wolf hide whose lightning runs into the ground, shield walls that link into a wall of light; plains knights in light armour with a running horse burnt into the plates that flickers in the charge, horsehair tassels; pearl-coast princes in sharkskin armour set with a hundred glowing pearls; wolf-eared thunder hunters in close hide with a short cape fringed in wolf teeth; plains hunters wearing an iron-hide wolf king's pelt; armour, helm and gauntlets cut from one beast so its element shows, fire-mane hide that sparks underfoot; kings with a glowing beast core in the crown.
万兽中: no gunpowder, no firearms. Mead-hall warbands: leather armour, ash spears, javelins and linden round shields painted with the home mountain, black iron mountain clasps and twisted arm rings holding a faint core-light; heroic weapons that grow with the beasts they slay, a dark-red blade from the mother furnace still hot for days, a longbow whose arrowhead burns deeper gold the longer it is drawn; elven wardens in forest-coloured clothes that change with the season, wood elves with vine bracers and bark shoes; forge-heart dwarves in heavy leather aprons and iron-toed boots with great hammers and rune-struck shields; a white bone sword in a carved stone scabbard; fire-mane wolf hide that throws sparks when its wearer runs.
万兽前: no gunpowder, no firearms. Heroes wear the beast they killed: the whole pelt as armour, the head as helm or hood, forepaws knotted across the chest, its element still alive, lightning crawling in leopard fur at night, frost breathing from an ice-mane wolf skin; hall warriors in iron scale shirts like fish scales under a bearskin over one shoulder, iron-rimmed round shields painted with a red branch; steppe queens in scale-hide armour over red-ochre felt with belts of gold plaques; weapons made of the beast, a frost-mammoth-tusk greatsword cold even in summer, an ash spear whose frost never melts, fire-mane bone swords that throw a tongue of flame; a polished bronze mirror shield holding a pair of closed stone eyes; hunt leaders with a sealed silver core-jar at the belt.
祭火: no gunpowder, no firearms, no kingdoms and almost no metal. Bone-tipped wooden spears and fire-hardened shafts, stone and bone arrowheads, hide shields, thick hide chest guards sewn on outside; arrowheads ground from salvaged iron of a fallen-god ruin with a dull ember glow; night fighters charging with torches wrapped in pale-silver shards that burn cold white and drive beasts back; hunters in white wolf pelts with the head as hood and yew longbows taller than themselves; the few who slew a great beast wear its hide and its element; a soot-black clay pot with a live ember on a cord at the neck; late in the age a dwarf-forged iron blade, or an elven warden's longbow and grey-green cloak.
